question: If sin (A + B) = (sqrt 3)/(2) {and} cos (A-B) = (sqrt 3)/(2) then which of the following will be possible values of A and B?
solution:
**Given:**

sin (A + B) = (√ 3)/(2) {and} cos (A-B) = (√ 3)/(2)

**Calculation:**

(A + B) = sin⁻¹(√3/2)

A + B = 60°

Then,

(A - B) = cos⁻¹(√3/2)

A - B = 30°

Solving,

**∴ A = 45° and B = 15°**
